note: Navigation paths change over time. Reports present them as guidance and link to the provider's own documentation.

dns_providers.name: DreamHost
dns_providers.edit_dns: Sign in to the DreamHost panel, open Websites → DNS (Domains → Manage Domains → DNS on older panels), choose the domain and use "Add Record" (custom DNS record).
dns_providers.dnssec: DreamHost has not historically offered DNSSEC signing for zones it hosts; check DreamHost's current documentation. If it is unavailable, DNSSEC requires moving the zone's DNS hosting to a provider that signs zones (for example Cloudflare, Amazon Route 53 or Google Cloud DNS) and then adding the DS record at the registrar.

dns_providers.name: Cloudflare
dns_providers.edit_dns: In the Cloudflare dashboard select the domain, open DNS → Records and choose "Add record".
dns_providers.dnssec: In the Cloudflare dashboard open DNS → Settings and select "Enable DNSSEC". Cloudflare then shows the DS record values to add at the registrar.

dns_providers.name: Amazon Route 53
dns_providers.edit_dns: In the AWS console open Route 53 → Hosted zones, select the domain and choose "Create record".
dns_providers.dnssec: In Route 53 open the hosted zone, choose DNSSEC signing → Enable DNSSEC signing (this creates a key-signing key backed by AWS KMS), then add the DS record shown to the registrar.

dns_providers.name: GoDaddy DNS
dns_providers.edit_dns: In GoDaddy open Domain Portfolio, select the domain, choose DNS and then "Add New Record".
dns_providers.dnssec: GoDaddy offers DNSSEC on its Premium DNS product: Domain Portfolio → the domain → DNS → DNSSEC.

dns_providers.name: Google Cloud DNS
dns_providers.edit_dns: In the Google Cloud console open Network services → Cloud DNS, select the zone and choose "Add standard" record set.
dns_providers.dnssec: In Cloud DNS open the zone, set DNSSEC to On, then add the DS record shown under "Registrar setup" at the registrar.

dns_providers.name: Namecheap BasicDNS
dns_providers.edit_dns: In Namecheap open Domain List → Manage next to the domain → Advanced DNS → "Add New Record".
dns_providers.dnssec: In Namecheap open Domain List → Manage → Advanced DNS and switch DNSSEC on.

dns_providers.name: Azure DNS
dns_providers.edit_dns: In the Azure portal open DNS zones, select the zone and choose "+ Record set".
dns_providers.dnssec: In the Azure portal open the DNS zone, choose DNSSEC → Enable, then add the DS record at the registrar.

dns_providers.name: DigitalOcean DNS
dns_providers.edit_dns: In the DigitalOcean control panel open Networking → Domains, select the domain and create the record.
dns_providers.dnssec: DigitalOcean DNS does not currently sign zones; DNSSEC requires a DNS provider that does.

default_dns_provider.name: your DNS hosting provider
default_dns_provider.edit_dns: Open the control panel of the provider that hosts the domain's DNS (the nameservers listed in this report) and add or edit the record there.
default_dns_provider.dnssec: Enable DNSSEC signing at the DNS hosting provider, then add the DS record it gives you at the registrar.

mail_providers.name: Google Workspace
mail_providers.dkim_steps: In the Google Admin console open Apps → Google Workspace → Gmail → Authenticate email, select the domain, generate a 2048-bit key with the selector "google", publish the TXT record it shows at google._domainkey.{domain}, wait for DNS to propagate and select "Start authentication".

mail_providers.name: Microsoft 365
mail_providers.dkim_steps: In the Microsoft Defender portal open Email & collaboration → Policies & rules → Threat policies → Email authentication settings → DKIM, select the domain, publish the two CNAME records it shows (selector1._domainkey and selector2._domainkey) and enable signing.

mail_providers.name: Zoho Mail
mail_providers.dkim_steps: In the Zoho Mail Admin Console open Domains → the domain → Email configuration → DKIM, add a selector, publish the TXT record it shows and select Verify.

mail_providers.name: Proton Mail
mail_providers.dkim_steps: In Proton Mail settings open Domain names → the domain → DKIM and publish the three CNAME records shown.

mail_providers.name: Fastmail
mail_providers.dkim_steps: Publish the fm1, fm2 and fm3 ._domainkey CNAME records shown in Fastmail Settings → Domains.

mail_providers.name: DreamHost Mail
mail_providers.dkim_steps: DreamHost signs outgoing mail with DKIM automatically when its mail service and DNS are both used; confirm the dreamhost._domainkey record exists in the DreamHost DNS panel.

default_mail_provider.name: your email provider
default_mail_provider.dkim_steps: Enable DKIM signing in your email provider's admin console and publish the selector record it gives you at <selector>._domainkey.{domain}.

spf_include_services.relay.mailchannels.net: MailChannels (relay used by many shared web hosts)

txt_token_services.google-site-verification: Google Search Console / Google Workspace domain verification

registrars.name: GoDaddy
registrars.lock: In GoDaddy open Domain Portfolio, select the domain, open Domain Settings and turn Domain Lock (transfer lock) on.
registrars.renew: In GoDaddy open Domain Portfolio, select the domain and turn Auto-renew on; confirm the payment method is current.
registrars.ds: In GoDaddy open Domain Portfolio → the domain → DNS → DNSSEC → Add DS record.

registrars.name: Namecheap
registrars.lock: In Namecheap open Domain List → Manage → Sharing & Transfer and set Domain Lock to locked.
registrars.renew: In Namecheap open Domain List and switch Auto-Renew on for the domain.
registrars.ds: In Namecheap open Domain List → Manage → Advanced DNS → DNSSEC and add the DS record.

registrars.name: Cloudflare Registrar
registrars.lock: Cloudflare Registrar locks domains against transfer by default; confirm under Domain Registration → Manage Domains → Configuration.
registrars.renew: Cloudflare Registrar renews automatically; confirm the billing method under Domain Registration.
registrars.ds: Cloudflare adds the DS record automatically when DNSSEC is enabled for a domain registered with it.

registrars.name: Squarespace Domains
registrars.lock: In Squarespace Domains open the domain → Registration settings and confirm the transfer lock is on.
registrars.renew: In Squarespace Domains open the domain → Billing and turn auto-renew on.
registrars.ds: In Squarespace Domains open the domain → DNS → DNSSEC to add the DS record.

registrars.name: DreamHost
registrars.lock: In the DreamHost panel open Domains → Registrations and enable the transfer lock for the domain.
registrars.renew: In the DreamHost panel open Domains → Registrations and turn auto-renew on.
registrars.ds: Add the DS record through DreamHost support or the registration settings for the domain.

registrars.name: Gandi
registrars.lock: In Gandi open Domain → the domain → Transfer and enable the transfer lock.
registrars.renew: In Gandi open Domain → the domain → Overview and enable automatic renewal.
registrars.ds: In Gandi open Domain → the domain → DNSSEC and add the key.

default_registrar.name: the domain's registrar
default_registrar.lock: In the registrar's control panel enable the transfer lock (clientTransferProhibited), sometimes called Domain Lock or Registrar Lock.
default_registrar.renew: In the registrar's control panel enable auto-renew and confirm the payment method and contact email are current.
default_registrar.ds: In the registrar's control panel open the DNSSEC settings for the domain and add the DS record supplied by the DNS host.
